name: stalwart
description: Stalwart Mail Server — JMAP webmail backend (jmap.diegonmarcos.com)

compose._doc_post_hook: v0.16 activate.sh: Step A creates any account declared in #users that is missing from Stalwart's registry (x:Account/set, create-only), then ensures per-user mailbox hierarchy (4 parents + 10 leaves from mail-rules-general.json::folders+folders_ui) + uploads + activates default.sieve. Idempotent. DOMAIN creation is still owned by stalwart-cli apply (manual recovery-mode bootstrap); account creation no longer is.

_doc_recovery_mode: First-boot v0.16 bootstrap toggle. Set true to inject STALWART_RECOVERY_MODE=1 + STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN=admin:${ADMIN_PASSWORD} into the container's env so v0.16 wipes settings + accepts admin login. After running `stalwart-cli apply --file export.json` + recreating listeners, flip back to false and redeploy. The container reads JMAP-object state from RocksDB on production boot.

docker._doc: The upstream Stalwart server image is pulled as-is (containers.app.image); the only thing built here is the JMAP filter-view sorter sidecar, compiled from src/crate.

native_build._doc_builder_image: In-container multi-stage compile so the binary is always the target arch, never the CI host's. app_dir keeps the build context to the crate alone — src/ also holds secrets.yaml and the config templates, none of which the compiler needs.
native_build._doc_apt: rustls does the TLS, so no libssl — ca-certificates only, and even that is belt-and-braces since the JMAP peer is reached over the docker bridge with verification disabled.

primary._doc_security_import: Dedicated rate-limit zone (security_jmap -> zone jmap, declared in infra-sec_caddy build.json security_snippets). A real JMAP sync is ~24+ Email/get calls plus query paging per pass; the shared global zone is 100/min/IP, so a sync eats 429s exactly like the MCP session-start starvation fixed in 12e9766e. max_upload 50MB matches Stalwart's advertised maxSizeUpload (the global request_limits caps bodies at 10MB, silently rejecting uploads the session JSON promises).
primary._doc_root_response_json_removed: Initially tried serving a STATIC session JSON at jmap.diegonmarcos.com/ to bypass Stalwart's :2443 port leak in apiUrl/downloadUrl/etc. BROKE LTT.rs because the static JSON has empty accounts: {} — JMAP clients NEED the authenticated per-user response which only Stalwart can generate (it includes the user's account ID, capabilities per account, etc.). The :2443 leak is a real Stalwart limitation but reverting to runtime session is the lesser evil. Static-JSON approach is preserved in caddyfile.nix root_response_json schema for non-stateful endpoints (where applicable).
primary._doc_l4_ports: Stalwart serves JMAP via jmap.diegonmarcos.com (HTTPS reverse_proxy to :2443) and classical IMAPS/SMTPS via SNI on :443 → its own :2993/:2465 listeners. These two SNI routes used to be declared in user-comm_tools-maddy/build.json even though Stalwart terminates them; moved here so that retiring Maddy's directory cannot silently delete the live mail endpoints. Maddy keeps only :25.

l4_ports.comment: IMAPS via SNI on :443 -> STALWART :2993 (2026-09-02). Maddy :993 (go-imap v1) advertises no CONDSTORE/QRESYNC/UIDPLUS, which forces clients into a full flag rescan of every synced folder each poll -- measured on-device: 9355 UID FLAGS fetches per 15-min pass, all night, phone dead at 04:49. Stalwart :2993 advertises CONDSTORE+QRESYNC+UIDPLUS+IMAP4rev2. The earlier objection to :2993 (IMAP clients see Stalwart's ENTIRE 1*-9* + A*-F* tree because JMAP and IMAP share one store) is mitigated by the subscription policy in mail-rules-profile-diego.json folder_options: only INBOX + the F* sender folders are subscribed, and clients honouring LSUB/subscriptions see the intended menu. Maddy keeps :25 inbound and its store stays intact for rollback: revert this upstream to oci-mail:993.
SMTPS via SNI on :443 → Stalwart :2465 (Maddy's :465 is legacy)

well_known._doc: JMAP autoconfig per RFC 8620: clients enter me@diegonmarcos.com and look up the apex /.well-known/jmap. Caddy proxies to Stalwart (passes the Authorization header through), Stalwart issues a relative 307 → /jmap/session, client re-issues to apex which Caddy proxies for /jmap/* (well_known sibling below). The PER-USER session JSON returned by Stalwart includes the user's accounts list (which LTT.rs and others require). The static JSON at jmap.diegonmarcos.com/ is for clients that bypass autoconfig and probe the discoverable hostname directly — but autoconfig clients NEED the authenticated Stalwart session.
well_known._doc_rewrite_to: Serve the session AT the discovery URL instead of making the client chase Stalwart's relative 307 (Location: /jmap/session). The redirect is legal and was the original design, but a client that mishandles a RELATIVE Location never arrives: Cloud-Mail failed 2026-09-01 with 'EndpointNotFoundException: Unable to fetch session object' while curl -L against the same URL returned a valid session in ~1.3s. Same upstream, same Authorization passthrough, same per-user session JSON — one less hop for every JMAP client, not a patch for one.
well_known.comment: JMAP autoconfig — proxies to Stalwart (preserves per-user session)

well_known._doc: Follow-through for Stalwart's relative redirect from /.well-known/jmap → /jmap/session. Path wildcard.
well_known.comment: JMAP API follow-through (matches relative redirect from /.well-known/jmap)

well_known._doc: Bare-host shortcut: clients that hit https://jmap.diegonmarcos.com/ (no path) get a 308 to /.well-known/jmap so the JMAP session JSON is reachable at any of three equivalent URLs — bare host, /.well-known/jmap, apex /.well-known/jmap. Relies on the proxy-route well_known graft (caddyfile.nix mkProxyRoute filtering wellKnownRoutes by target_domain). Mailtemi and similar clients that probe the bare subdomain hostname work without manual URL entry.
well_known.comment: Bare host → JMAP discovery URL (308 redirect)

app._doc_dual_bind: Phase 4 of public-surface collapse: each port dual-binds on wg0 (10.0.0.3) AND wg-public (10.1.0.3). Caddy on oci-analytics reaches mail ports via wg-public mesh; legacy clients on wg0 keep working unchanged. compose.nix expands `bind` arrays into one host-port mapping per IP.
app._doc_container_port: v0.16 binds protocols on STANDARD ports inside the container (SMTP:25, IMAPS:993, SMTPS:465, HTTPS:443, Sieve:4190) — listeners are not configurable in v0.16 schema. We map host_offset → container_standard so external clients keep using offset ports (maddy owns the standard ones on the host network until decommissioned).

extra_ports.desc: Plain-HTTP JMAP on the MESH ONLY (host:2080 → stalwart:8080). Bound on wg0/wg-public, never on a public interface: .app is WireGuard-only and WG already encrypts, so the mesh endpoint stalwart.mesh.diegonmarcos.com is plain http (fleet convention, #1093). Cloud Mail and the fleet apps reach JMAP here first and fall back to the public jmap.diegonmarcos.com with the bearer.

resources._doc_limits: oci-mail is a VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro (1 OCPU, 954MiB). 2026-10-13 it ran load 6-10, io PSI ~78%, cpu PSI ~74%, with stalwart at 110-160% CPU and 105GB read in 21h, every mail container capped only by the 2G category default (i.e. by nothing on a 954MiB box). cpus 0.7 leaves 0.3 OCPU for maddy (the MX leg) whatever stalwart does. mem_limit is NOT the 256M first proposed: measured on the box the same day stalwart's anon commit was ~306MiB 30 min after a restart (130MiB resident + 176MiB swapped) and ~345MiB after 21h, and the fleet already learned that 256M on stalwart is a thrash wall (_shared/docker.nix: 2909 memory.max breach events on oci-apps). restart is "no" fleet-wide, so an OOM kill here is not a blip -- it is webmail/IMAP down until someone notices. 384M sits above the measured peak with docker's default 2x memswap behind it. Gate: _shared/test-mail-stack-limits.mjs.
resources._doc_file_rereads: 2026-11-18 16:20 UTC oci-mail: io PSI some 61.6 / full 13.4, ~12MB/s file refaults (pgpgin 12188KB/s, workingset_refault_file 393/s), stalwart 1474MB cumulative cgroup reads, swap not involved, stalwart ~70MiB resident. Cause: the stalwart-sorter filter pass asked Email/get for bodyStructure on every in-scope message (~11.7k) every pass, and v0.16.5 serves bodyStructure by reading the whole raw blob (crates/jmap/src/email/get.rs needs_body), so each pass read the entire mailbox off the boot disk. Fixed in the sorter (src/crate/src/filters.rs AttachTypeCache: bodyStructure once per message per process, only for attach_type views). Stalwart-side settings checked against the v0.16.5 registry schema and left at defaults because none of them re-reads on a cadence: the RocksDb store exposes only blobSize/bufferSize/poolWorkers (no block-cache knob); Search indexes on ingest (indexBatchSize 100), not on a timer; SpamClassifier trains every 12h from a 1024-sample reservoir; DataRetention purges run once a day (00:00/02:00/04:00); the queue wakes on due events; the tracer is Stdout at info (writes, not reads). mem_limit stays 384M: ~70MiB resident leaves ~300MiB of headroom, and the 704MiB mail total has no room to raise it. Gate: _shared/test-mail-stack-limits.mjs B1-B4.
resources._doc_reservation: 32M -> 128M (2026-11-18). Docker maps reservations.memory to cgroup v2 memory.low: under host pressure the kernel reclaims everyone else's unprotected page cache before stalwart's protected part. 128M covers the ~70MiB resident plus ~58MiB of hot RocksDB index/property pages, so those stop being evicted and re-read. It reserves nothing up front and caps nothing. Mail-stack reservations total 192M of 954M. Gate: _shared/test-mail-stack-limits.mjs R1-R3.
resources._doc_reservation_192: 128M -> 192M (2026-11-18 23:08). After the sorter, puller and maddy fixes, oci-mail was back to PSI avg300 34 with stalwart the only cgroup reading (950KB/s over 10s) and its logs showing only light SMTP (3 inbound, 3 queue retries). 128M of memory.low covered the ~100MiB of anon/active memory plus ~28MiB of cache, so stalwart's RocksDB SST pages beyond that were still reclaimed by host pressure and read again on the next lookup. RocksDB's block cache is not configurable in v0.16.5 (see _doc_file_rereads), so the page cache IS its block cache, and memory.low is the declarative way to keep it. 192M is half the unchanged 384M ceiling. Mail-stack reservations total 320M of 954M (stalwart 192, maddy 96, sorter 16, puller 16), at the R3 budget.

sorter._doc_image: Was python:3-alpine running a bind-mounted jmap-sorter.py. Now a compiled binary: the rules schema is parsed and validated once at startup, so a malformed or unknown predicate stops the container instead of silently producing an empty filter folder.

resources._doc_mem_limit: Measured 2026-10-13: cgroup peak 10MiB, anon ~1MiB. 64M is 6x that.

_doc_users: The `admin` entry is the ADMIN PRINCIPAL: src/flake.nix derives adminEmail/adminPassEnv from it and configs/activate.sh authenticates every registry upsert (allowed-ip, MTA routes, throttles) as that account. In v0.16.5 admin-ness is a field on the account object itself — `roles: {"@type": "Admin"}` — not a separate principal record; an account with roles=User authenticates fine but gets no `urn:stalwart:jmap` entry in its JMAP session's primaryAccounts and can read nothing from the registry. Verified live 2026-09-04: only `me` (roles Admin) and `no-reply` (roles User) existed in Stalwart's store — `mailadmin`/`yo`/`42` were declared here but had NEVER been created, because account creation was not part of the deploy, so those three existed in maddy alone and could not log into cloud-webmail (which authenticates against Stalwart JMAP, not maddy). That is why cloud-mail-mcp's STALWART_ADMIN_USER pointed at admin@diegonmarcos.com and 401'd; it now points at me@diegonmarcos.com. Since 2026-09-05 this list is the single source of truth for BOTH stores: activate.sh Step A creates any missing account via x:Account/set. It is CREATE-ONLY — an existing account is never updated, because secrets are stored hashed (so every ship would blind-reset the password) and because writing roles could demote the only Admin and lock the hook out of the registry. Rotating a password or changing a role on an EXISTING account therefore still needs a deliberate manual x:Account/set update.
_doc_mta_routes: Outbound SMTP routes for Stalwart's MTA. OCI Free Tier blocks outbound :25/:465/:587 from VMs, so direct MX delivery fails — every route must be a Relay to a paid SMTP service (OCI Email Delivery, AWS SES, etc.). activate.sh maps these into JMAP MtaRoute objects via /jmap/ + the urn:stalwart:jmap capability. Credentials are referenced by env-var NAME only (auth_username_env / auth_secret_env); actual values live in secrets.yaml.

mta_routes.name: oci-relay
mta_routes.description: OCI Email Delivery (eu-marseille-1) — primary outbound relay; SMTP creds shared with maddy (same vault user/pass, region-bound)

mta_routes.name: maddy-relay
mta_routes.description: Maddy submission co-located on oci-mail. Selected when the envelope MAIL FROM is me+maddy@diegonmarcos.com (the cloud-webmail 'me@ (via Maddy)' identity's return-path). Maddy strips the +tag, DKIM-signs (selector default), then relays to OCI — giving an independent send leg that still shows From: me@. Auth reuses the me@ account: username is the plain mailbox address, password is the shared ME_PASSWORD (identical on both servers). allow_invalid_certs because we reach Maddy by its WG IP, whose cert CN is mail.diegonmarcos.com (WG-internal, so skipping name-verify is safe).

_doc_allowed_ips: IP ranges trusted by Stalwart's fail2ban/auth-ban (v0.16.5 stores these as AllowedIp registry objects; the old config.toml server.allowed-ip is dead because config.toml is not loaded). activate.sh upserts these via JMAP so internal clients on the WG mesh + docker bridge are never banned. Keep in sync with the wg0 /24 and the stalwart_default bridge /16.

delivery_ledger._doc: #1802 delivery-status ledger. Stalwart's own records of every authenticated submission and its delivery, streamed to the fleet mail API (infra-api_cloudy-apps-communication-mcp, oci-apps 10.0.0.6:3103) over wg0. Two registry objects, upserted by configs/apply-delivery-ledger.py from activate.sh Step I, matched by url (neither object has a name): (1) a WebHook (telemetry subscriber) carrying the queue/delivery/DSN/sender-auth events listed below as JSON batches — the source for received, delivered and per-recipient results; (2) an MtaHook at the DATA stage, enabled only for authenticated submissions and for null-sender mail (bounces/DSNs) — the only Stalwart record that ties the RFC 5322 Message-ID, header From and SASL login to the queue id, and the path remote DSNs arrive on. tempFailOnError is false and the API answers accept before doing any work, so the ledger being down never delays or bounces mail; it only leaves a gap in the ledger. No shared secret: the API accepts these two paths only from oci-mail's WG addresses (WireGuard binds the source IP to the peer key). Schema verified against stalwartlabs/stalwart v0.16.5 crates/registry/src/schema/structs.rs (WebHook, MtaHook) and crates/trc event names.

_doc_tests: Registered #502 (this repo's tester CI only runs what a build.json's `tests` key names, per .github/scripts/run-service-tests.sh -- an unnamed tester sits in the tree, executable, and reached by nothing, same pattern cloud-u-android's #368 found 44 times over). mail-rules was a golden+structural suite for derive-mail-rules.ts with no build.json anywhere pointing at it, so it had never run in CI despite existing since #269. It pins the declared mail folder tree (parent/child nesting, not just names) and the Sieve/maddy artifact derivation; #502 added the structural assertions for the Alerts/noAlerts split, the 24 House -> F0 move (with real de-dup), and the CLOUD -> 40 C3 renumber.
